div.head: II Em 7
div.ab: Witan scylan fæhðe sectan: ærest æfter folcrihte slaga sceal his forspecan on hand syllan, ⁊ se forspeca magum, þæt se slaga wylle betan wið mægðe.
Witan scylon fæhðe sectan: ærest æfter folcrihte slaga sceal his forspecan on hand syllan, ⁊ se forspeca magum, þæt se slaga wille betan wið mægðe.
Sapientum est sedare factionem: Inprimis iuxta rectam populi lagam debet prolocutor occisoris in manum dare cognationi, quod rectum ei per omnia faciet.
[Be fæhþe.] Witan scylon fæhðe sectan: ærest æfter folcrihte slaga sceal his forspecan on hand syllan ⁊ se forspeca magum, þæt se slaga wille betan wið mægðe.

(Über Rachefehde. Ld) Notable sollen Fehde beilegen: erstens soll nach Volksrecht der Todtschläger seinem Fürsprech, und dieser Fürsprech den Verwandten [des Erschlagenen] in die Hand geloben, dass der Todtschläger gegenüber jener Sippe Busse zahlen wolle.

(Of blood-feud. Ld) The witan are to settle feuds: first, according to folk-law, the slayer is to give a pledge into the hand of his advocate, and this advocate [is to give one] to the kinsmen [of the slain man], that the slayer will pay compensation to that kindred.

The authorities must put a stop to vendettas. First, according to public law, the slayer shall give security to his advocate, and the advocate to the kinsmen [of the slain man], that he (the slayer) will make reparation to the kindred.

Leading men must settle feuds: First, according to the common law the slayer must give a pledge to his advocate, and the advocate to the kinsmen, that the slayer is willing to pay compensation to the kindred.

note.seg: Der Inhalt dieses Kapitels steht teilweise auch in Wer, und zwar wahrscheinlich (s. u. 7, 3⁴) in mindestens Einem Punkte, der Fechtstrafe, vollständiger. Diese forderte II Em 3 in jedem Falle, also gewiss auch hier. Diese Halbzeile überspringt der Archetyp von II Em infolge des mit Vorigem und Folgendem gleichlautenden Beginnes. Die übrigen Zusätze in Wer scheinen mir spätere, private Erklärung.—Das Wort grið erscheint—abgesehen von EGu—hier zuerst in den Gesetzen; ein zweites Nord. Lehnwort ist sehtan; vgl. o. II 636 Sp. 3 Z. 13 und Toller 857. Daher meint Steenstrup zu weitgehend, das ganze Kapitel folge Nordischem Rechte; Danelag 182⁴. 298. Auch die allerdings veränderte stilistische Form zwingt nicht, in 7 ein fremdes Anhängsel zu sehen, das etwa nur des verwandten Inhalts wegen hierher geriet

The content of this chapter is also found in part in Wer, and indeed probably (see below 7, 3⁴) more completely in at least one point, the penalty for fighting. II Em 3 demanded this in every case, and so certainly here too. The archetype of II Em skips this half-line because it begins with the same words as what precedes and what follows. The other additions in Wer seem to me a later, private explanation.—Apart from EGu, the word grið appears here for the first time in the laws; a second Norse loanword is sehtan; cf. above II 636 col. 3 l. 13 and Toller 857. Steenstrup therefore goes too far in holding that the whole chapter follows Norse law; Danelag 182⁴. 298. Nor does the stylistic form, altered though it admittedly is, compel us to see in 7 a foreign appendage that found its way here perhaps only because of its related content

Vielleicht sind besonders ‘Gerichtsobere, Schiedsmannen, Rechtsanordner’ gemeint; s. Wb: wita 5. Auch das Festland kennt amtliche Vermittler der Totschlagsühne, . bisweilen Ratmannen; Frauenstädt Blutrache 48. 106.—Ld's Lesung settan ist vielleicht nur Druckfehler. Zwar nimmt Toller 868 XI sie auf, führt aber keinen sonstigen Beleg für diese Bed. an. Der Archetyp las sehtan; streiche I 188 §§.—Vgl. Gl Schiedsgericht 9a ff.

Perhaps ‘heads of courts, arbitrators, regulators of law’ are especially meant; see Wb: wita 5. The Continent too knows official mediators of the composition for homicide, sometimes councillors; Frauenstädt Blutrache 48. 106.—Ld's reading settan is perhaps only a misprint. Toller 868 XI does admit it, but cites no other instance of this meaning. The archetype read sehtan; delete I 188 §§.—Cf. Gl Schiedsgericht 9a ff.
Dieser Vorsprech (s. d. Gl 4), hier nicht Bürge, wie Rieger Altsä. Leseb. 259 meint, noch auch Schützer oder Plädierer oder Anwalt, kommt auch anderwärts vor
This advocate (see that word in Gl 4) — here not a surety, as Rieger Altsä. Leseb. 259 thinks, nor a protector, pleader or attorney either — occurs elsewhere too
Vgl. Gl Hand 2; Versprechen 2a; Blutrache 15b; Sippe 24. 26
Cf. Gl Hand 2; Versprechen 2a; Blutrache 15b; Sippe 24. 26
Cf. Be Wergilde and see Seebohm, Tribal Custom, p. 356 ff.; Phillpotts, Kindred and Clan, p. 219 ff.

Liebermann translates ‘Notable’ and says in his notes (iii. p. 128) that perhaps ‘Gerichtsobere, Schiedsmannen, Rechtsanordner’ in particular are meant. He points out that official mediators (‘amtliche Vermittler’) were known on the continent (see Frauenstädt, Blutrache, pp. 47, 106), but the reference here seems more general, namely, to ‘men in authority’ simply, not to any definitely appointed arbitrators.
Sectan is a Scandinavian loan word, cf. Norse sætta, to reconcile, make peace among.
Cf. the Norse law-term handsal and the modern German phrase in die Hand versprechen, to promise something solemnly.

It is difficult to determine whether the forspeca is a person who is permanently responsible for the slayer (i.e. his borh), or whether he is merely a friend whom he has induced to act on his behalf. Liebermann takes the latter view.
